Guys, I've been bitten,.. by the running bug that is. I started last year doing C25K and got hooked quickly. My best 5k is 23:30 (race) and my current fastest long run is 10k at 56:34. I would like to slowly train up to half marathon which gives me 16 weeks.

Does it make sense to extend the usual 12 week plans to 16 weeks or is there something magic about sticking to 12 weeks ( rest periods and all ). Anyone have any good online planners for this distance?

Edit: Found a good site: my.asics.com and have started my plan there.
Half marathon in December, online planner?

First, those are some great times for a beginner just starting with the C25K!

The Higdon plans are the most popular for finishing a first half marathon. I think having 16 instead of 12 weeks makes you better off. You can make the training more gradual. He mentions what you can do if you have more than 12 weeks:

Do you have more than a dozen weeks before your selected Half Marathon? Lengthen the schedule; take 18 or even 24 weeks to prepare. Repeat the week just completed before moving up to the next level. Don't be afraid to insert "stepback" weeks, where you actually cut your distance every second or third week to gather forces for the next push upward. To see how this "stepback" approach works, check out the training schedules for the marathon distance.

So you can build in repeated weeks, which will be smart because it will slow down the progression of how much distance you are adding per week.
